answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate combined with 14-day renewal deadline and high line utilization (94%) rules out defer_decision and add_second_source (too slow to onboard). Switching to the low-cost vendor (memory_c2) is rejected because their 75% SLA miss rate creates unacceptable delivery risk when the assembly line has zero buffer. Renewing incumbent alone leaves the 18% gap unresolved. Instead, aggressive renegotiation leverages memory_c4's proven result (real margin recovered through benchmarking) and memory_c6's insight (multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing). Verify memory_c4 to confirm the specific negotiation tactics that moved the incumbent, and memory_c2 to quantify the low-cost vendor's SLA performance and confirm they remain unsuitable as primary source. This approach targets cost recovery within the incumbent relationship, eliminates the delivery risk of sole-source switching, and preserves the option to add second source in the next cycle if the 18% target cannot be negotiated. The incumbent's stability (memory_c1) supports continuity during the negotiation window.
